newsitem.title: USA: "Lost World" tramples on U.S. box office rivals.
newsitem.headline: "Lost World" tramples on U.S. box office rivals.

text.p: "The Lost World: Jurassic Park" easily topped the U.S. box office for the second consecutive weekend, earning more than the rest of the top 10 combined, according to studio estimates released on Sunday.

The Steven Spielberg dinosaur romp took home an estimated $32.6 million for the Friday to Sunday period, bringing its total to $140 million. The next nine grossed about $32.0 million altogether, said Exhibitor Relations, which collects the studios' estimates. Final data will be issued on Monday.
Holding in second was the Meg Ryan/Matthew Broderick romantic comedy, "Addicted To Love," with $6.4 million. The movie's 10-day total stands at $20.3 million.

The top 10 contained three new entries, none of which performed strongly. "Gone Fishin'," a comedy starring Joe Pesci and Danny Glover, opened in third with about $5.5 million. The Michael Richards comedy "Trial and Error" was fourth with $5.0 million, while the ensemble romantic comedy "'Til There Was You" debuted in 10th with $1.3 million.
Rounding out the top five was the Bruce Willis sci-fi picture ,"The Fifth Element," which earned $4.0 million. After four weekends, it has earned about $51.5 million.

"The Lost World: Jurassic Park" is released by Universal Pictures, a unit of Seagram Co. Ltd.. "Addicted To Love" is released by Warner Bros, a unit of Time Warner Inc. . "Gone Fishin'" is released by Walt Disney Co. . "Trial and Error" is released by Time Warner's New Line Cinema, a unit of Time Warner. "'Til There Was You" is released by Paramount Pictures, a unit of Viacom Inc.. "The Fifth Element" is released by Columbia Pictures, a unit of Sony Corp..
